Assume full AC. Let $N\cong D^2\times S^1$ be an oriented solid torus in the interior of an oriented smooth 3-manifold, let $K$ be its core with any integral framing, and let $U$ be a small meridian of $K$ with the zero framing given by its meridian disk. Simultaneous framed surgery on $K$ and $U$ returns a solid torus diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the original identification on $\partial N$. Thus inserting or removing this pair preserves the ambient manifold relative to the complement of $N$, including external collars and boundary parametrizations. An embedded colored ribbon graph avoiding $N$ is fixed. No assertion is made that a graph traversing $N$ is fixed, or that this operation belongs to a complete relative move list.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold with collared boundary $\partial W=\partial_0W\sqcup\partial_1W$, let $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_1W$ be an attaching embedding of a $k$-handle and let $\psi:S^k\times D^{n-k-1}\to\partial_1(W\cup_\varphi h^k)$ be an attaching embedding of a $(k+1)$-handle attached after it, where $0\le k\le n-1$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Assume AC. Let a finite smooth relative four-dimensional handle movie be based on a compact oriented three-manifold $N$, with its boundary product collar fixed. Choose a framed replacement arc in $N$ joining its feet and carry it by the foot isotopy; assume other birth/death supports miss its tube. Here $O3$ is a framed knot with its small disk-zero meridian. All framings and actual outgoing boundary maps are retained, and the boundary collar is fixed pointwise. The statement permits arbitrary homotopy class of the replacement arc and arbitrary finite signed traversals by the other strips. It is local conversion of the supplied movie, not its global existence.

Assume AC. In dimension $d\ge4$, a one-handle whose feet lie in the same connected lower stage can be replaced, by an interior framed circle surgery, with one $(d-2)$-handle. The statement retains the integral framing of $K$. In a two-handle trace every interior framed circle can be put in this form by the preceding circle lemma. Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold with boundary admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume AC. Let $(F_s,X_s)$ be the weak relative descending family of [[lem-relative-descending-path-with-finite-same-index-passages]] on a compact $d$-dimensional collared bordism. Its vertical product height and endpoint fields are fixed. Assume full AC. On a compact smooth collared bordism, keep the incoming and outgoing parametrizations as part of a finite elementary handle description. A generic adapted function path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]] induces a finite sequence of changes of its Morse-induced elementary handle descriptions: relative diffeomorphisms and isotopies of the framed attaching embeddings, changes of standard handle-coordinate frame, splitting/merging empty product bands, interchange of two independent disjoint framed attachments, and creation/removal of a geometrically cancelling adjacent-index pair. At every change retain the induced outgoing boundary map and carry every later attaching embedding and final boundary parametrization by it. Changes of descending field within a single elementary band alter its framed attaching embedding and outgoing map only by the corresponding isotopies. The birth cancellation has exactly one connecting trajectory. Disconnected bordisms, empty ends, and index $0/n$ pairs are included.

This is a comparison of parametrized elementary bands with their actual cancellation boundary maps retained. It does not suppress those maps, classify an arbitrary global path of descending fields by slides, or assert surgery/Kirby/coupon completeness.

Assume full AC. Let $q$ be an index-$k$ Morse critical point in dimension $n$, $1\le k\le n-1$, with fixed local coordinates and descending field $f=c-|u|^2+|v|^2$, $X=(2u,-2v)$, for $(u,v)\in\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$. Let $p$ be a higher critical point of the same index. Suppose a one-parameter family of the descending attaching-sphere sections of $p$ passes through the stable section of $q$ once, at one point, and transversely in the following sense: its $k-1$ sphere-patch directions and its parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $k$ unstable directions at the event. Assume all remaining attaching data are disjoint from the chosen local passage region; retain the joining band, lower regular level, and normal framing, and assume no intervening critical point between that region and the chosen lower level.

The two framed attaching embeddings obtained by transporting below $q$, before and after this isolated passage, differ by the signed framed band sum with a parallel of the attaching sphere of $q$. For $k=1$ this replaces one foot by a parallel of the other foot of $q$ along the band. For $1\le k\le n-2$ this is the handle slide of the existing definition and preserves the relative diffeomorphism type with all later attaching maps carried along. In particular $n=4,k=2$ gives the framed-link slide. For $n=3,k=2$, only the stated local surface band sum with its supplied embedded band is asserted; no higher-codimension band-existence contract is imported. No generic-family existence or global trajectory-completeness assertion is made.

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Its prescribed oriented rank-three normal framing is represented, up to homotopy and isotopy of its small tubular attaching embedding, by an integral rank-two framing in $N$ plus the level-normal line. More generally, freely homotopic embedded circles in a smooth manifold of dimension $d\ge4$ are isotopic whenever their homotopy lies in a prescribed relatively compact open set; the isotopy may be supported in that set. Every loop class in a three-manifold has an embedded representative avoiding a prescribed finite link.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. If $V,A_0,A_1$ are connected and $A_0,A_1$ are nonempty, there is such a relative presentation with no handles of index zero or $d$. No fundamental-group assumption or h-cobordism hypothesis is imposed.

Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold with prescribed boundary parametrizations and a fixed product collar $C\subset Y$. Surgery links lie in $\operatorname{Int}(Y\setminus C)$. For a framed link $L$, let $Y_L$ be its Dehn filling, with the canonical unchanged collar $C$, and let $E_L=Y\setminus\operatorname{Int}N(L)$ denote its exterior. The meridian of the $i$th filling solid torus is glued to the surgery-framed parallel $\lambda_i$ on $\partial N(L_i)$.

A decoration is a finite properly embedded oriented framed ribbon graph, with fixed abstract coupon set, actual coupon morphisms and band labels, fixed attachment order, and prescribed product ribbons in $C$ meeting only the designated marked boundary intervals. Colored graph isotopies keep all these collars, endpoints and labels fixed. Then:

1. Every decoration in $Y_L$ has a representative in $\operatorname{Int}(E_L)\cup C$, relative to its prescribed collar ribbons.
2. Two such exterior decorations that are isotopic as framed labeled graphs in $Y_L$ are connected by finitely many exterior framed colored graph isotopies and framed slides of open graph strands over the surgery parallels $\lambda_i$. Original coupons and colors remain fixed.
3. Suppose the **marked undecorated relative surgery calculus** holds in $Y$: every required collared bordism has a marked surgery presentation, and every specified orientation-preserving identification of two outputs, fixed pointwise on $C$, is realized up to isotopy relative to $C$ by a finite sequence of the canonical local undecorated moves $O1$ (a separated $\pm1$ unknot), $O2$ (a framed surgery-component band slide), $O3$ (a framed knot plus a small zero-framed meridian), and exterior link isotopies. The canonical move maps are the standard local filling identifications, identity outside their specified local neighborhoods. Under exactly this hypothesis, every marked decorated bordism admits an exterior decorated presentation, and two presentations of the same marked decoration are connected by the corresponding undecorated moves, exterior colored graph isotopies, and the open-colored-strand slides in (2).

The hypothesis in (3) concerns the **specified** output identification, not merely existence of some diffeomorphism. No undecorated completeness theorem is proved or assumed silently here. After surgery components are colored by $\Omega$, all the extra graph moves in this conclusion preserve the complete fixed-coupon evaluation by [[lem-kirby-color-full-band-slide-and-coupon-identity]]; the usual local $O1/O2/O3$ normalization identities are separate algebraic suppliers. Connectedness is not required.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $h_1,h_2$ be $k$-handles attached to $M\subseteq\partial_+W$ as in the slide definition, with $1\le k\le n-2$, and let $h_1'$ be a slide of $h_1$ over $h_2$ (the slid handle attached to $M$ by the band move). Then $W\cup_{f_1}h_1\cup_{f_2}h_2$ and $W\cup_{f_1'}h_1'\cup_{f_2}h_2$ are diffeomorphic relative to $\partial_0W$; more precisely there is a diffeomorphism supported in a neighbourhood of the two handles and the band region carrying the first presentation to the second. Consequently a handle slide does not change the diffeomorphism type of the presented manifold and may be performed on any of two equal-index handles.

Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds, with their boundaries identified with the same oriented surface $\Sigma$ in the bordism convention and with fixed compatible product collars. There is a finite framed link in $\operatorname{int}N$ whose surgery is diffeomorphic to $M$ with the prescribed external boundary parametrization. It may be realized as a four-dimensional two-handle trace with those marked horizontal faces and vertical collar $\Sigma\times[0,1]$. More generally this holds componentwise for a specified common component partition; empty input is treated by the empty union. In particular a fixed connected standard base with the required boundary may be chosen on each component, and a closed component may use $N=S^3$. An explicit connected standard base is the complement in $S^3$ of standard handlebodies placed in pairwise disjoint balls, one for each boundary component with its specified genus, with the given surface parametrizations attached to these boundary copies. This is relative surgery existence, not equivalence or completeness of surgery moves. Decorations may be carried by the resulting actual diffeomorphism; a complete decorated move theorem is a separate assertion.

Assume AC. Let $N$ be a connected nonempty compact oriented three-manifold and let $W_0,W_1$ be connected four-dimensional finite two-handle traces from that same fixed base. Their full common boundary $Y$ and all horizontal, external and corner collar identifications are marked. Suppose a connected compact oriented five-bordism $V$ between them is supplied with its full vertical product collar $Y\times I$ fixed. Then finitely many O3 insertions on each original framed link give two descriptions of the same actual four-dimensional two-handle trace $W_*$ from $N$, with the full marked boundary retained. Here each O3 insertion is a framed knot and its small disk-framed zero meridian, with its actual boundary-relative identification. No condition on any fundamental group is required. In conjunction with the projective-plane stabilization supplier, split signed unit-framed unknot insertions first supply such a $V$ whenever needed. This is a common-middle existence assertion; it does not assert that the two descriptions of $W_*$ are related by a complete O2/O3 movie.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge4$, and let $V$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional bordism with corners, horizontal faces $A_0,A_1$, and vertical face $B\times[0,1]$, with compatible product collar charts fixed. Here $\partial A_i=B\times\{i\}$. There are excellent Morse data with all critical points interior, equal to the specified height $t$ on a fixed smaller vertical product collar, zero and one on the horizontal faces with their prescribed inward collar models. They give a finite handle decomposition whose attaching thickenings lie in the interiors of horizontal levels, away from the fixed vertical collar, retaining the actual outgoing identification. Critical values may be ordered by index while this entire boundary height is fixed. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c\in(0,1)$, with no critical point of another index at $c$ and no other
critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be compact with $\partial N=\partial_-N\sqcup\partial_+N$, and let $f_N:N\to[0,1]$ be Morse, with $f_N^{-1}(1)=\partial_+N$ and $f_N=1-t$ on a critical-point-free outgoing collar. Attach a $k$-handle along an admissible framed embedding $h:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_+N$, obtaining $N'$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is a Morse $f':N'\to[0,1]$, equal to $f_N$ on the part of $N$ outside the outgoing collar strip $t<2\varepsilon$ and near $\partial_-N$, whose old critical points and critical values are unchanged and whose only new critical point has index $k$ and value $1-\varepsilon/2$. Its endpoint fibre at one is the new outgoing face, and $f'=1-t'$ on a smaller outgoing collar. Its handle attachment is the prescribed one, up to compatible collar and corner choices.

The height of the whole old outgoing face must be lowered before the new critical band is glued. Pointwise agreement on that face, or identification of every saddle level with a product attaching tube, is not asserted.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge1$, with fixed product collars, and let $f_0,f_1:W\to[0,1]$ be excellent adapted Morse functions equal to the same noncritical product height on those collars. There is a smooth path $F_s$ joining them, stationary near its parameter endpoints and fixed on smaller boundary collars, with finitely many exceptional parameters. Each exceptional parameter contains exactly one of: a corank-one interior birth/death with nonzero kernel cubic and nonzero parameter unfolding, or a transverse crossing of two nondegenerate critical values. All other critical points are nondegenerate, all other critical values are distinct, no two events share a parameter, and a birth value differs from every other critical value. The critical locus is a compact smooth curve whose parameter projection has only nondegenerate folds. Each fold creates or destroys two critical points of adjacent indices with distinct critical values. By a homotopy supported near each fold, preserving this event list and the endpoints, the path can further be put near that fold in smooth parameter-dependent spatial coordinates into the form

$$F_s=a(s)+b(s)u+c_0u^3+Q(y),\qquad b(0)=0,\quad b'(0)\ne0,\quad c_0>0,$$

where $Q$ is a fixed nondegenerate quadratic form in $n-1$ variables. Empty ends, disconnected $W$, and index $0/n$ pairs are allowed. This is a function-path statement with fixed product height; it has no boundary critical events and asserts no global descending-field or surgery-move theorem.

Assume full AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $d$-dimensional collared bordism, $d\ge1$, and let $f_s$ be a path supplied by [[lem-relative-one-parameter-morse-path-with-finite-events]], with the given noncritical height fixed on the spatial collars. Prescribe descending endpoint fields, stationary near the parameter ends, standard near their Morse critical points, and having no trajectories from index $i$ to index $j\ge i$. Morse–Smale endpoint fields suffice. Then there is a smooth descending family $X_s$ with those endpoint and collar values such that:

1. Near every fold it is the negative Euclidean gradient of the exact cubic model. At every regular critical point it has a smooth hyperbolic descending model. Near each same-index passage it may be taken to have the normalized linear Morse model at the destination.
2. No ordinary trajectory increases index. The entire family has finitely many same-index connecting trajectories; each occurs at a distinct parameter away from births and critical-value crossings. Each is a transverse parameter passage: on an incoming section at its destination, the $i-1$ source-sphere tangent directions together with the parameter direction map isomorphically onto the $i$-dimensional normal space of the stable section.
3. A sufficiently small parameter neighborhood of each birth contains no same-index trajectory. Between its two newborn critical points there is exactly the standard cancelling trajectory.
4. In successive one-critical elementary bands, the full framed attaching embeddings and actual outgoing boundary maps vary smoothly on each regular function chamber, including through positive-index-drop tangencies. The existing elementary birth and critical-value-crossing comparisons retain their actual outgoing maps, and their composition retains the terminal boundary parametrization.

Disconnected $W$, empty ends, and index $0/d$ births are allowed. This is an elementary-band assertion: it neither asserts slice-wise Morse–Smale transversality at positive index drops nor supplies parameterwise grouping of arbitrary based handle presentations by index or a global Kirby completeness theorem.

Assume AC. Let $(F_s,X_s)$ be the weak relative descending family of [[lem-relative-descending-path-with-finite-same-index-passages]] on a compact $d$-dimensional collared bordism. Its vertical product height and endpoint fields are fixed. There is a smooth family $g_s$ with the same critical points, indices and exact positive-affine cubic birth models, such that $X_sg_s<0$ off the critical points and all critical heights are ordered by index. The boundary height is unchanged. The family has finitely many simple same-index critical-value crossings, no triple values or simultaneous two crossings, and no such crossing at a same-index trajectory event or at a fold. The only other coincidences are the intended folds. The trajectories, their finite same-index passages, full framed local data and actual terminal identifications are retained. Positive-index-drop tangencies are allowed.

Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact smooth four-dimensional bordism with fixed horizontal faces, fixed vertical product height, and specified all-two-handle endpoint presentations. Apply the finite weak descending-path supplier and its parametric index grouping, with the endpoint fields prescribed from those presentations. Then there is a finite based framed mixed-handle movie joining the given endpoint presentations. Its elementary changes are framed isotopies, same-index handle slides (index3 read as the reverse index1 slide), cancelling adjacent-index births/deaths and commuting critical-value interchanges of disjoint attachments. Every higher attaching embedding and the complete terminal parametrization are carried by the actual outgoing comparisons. All supports fix the vertical boundary collar. No slicewise Morse–Smale condition at positive index drop is required.

Assume AC. Let $N,M$ be connected nonempty compact oriented smooth three-manifolds with their external boundary parametrizations and vertical product collar fixed. Let $W$ be a connected compact oriented four-bordism between them. Suppose two specified all-two-handle presentations of $W$ are joined by the finite index-grouped based mixed-handle movie of [[lem-index-grouped-relative-descending-paths-give-based-framed-handle-movies]], with its actual terminal maps. Intermediate four-dimensional traces may change by the displayed interior surgeries. No assumption that diffeomorphic four-dimensional two-handlebodies are two-equivalent is made. The construction works componentwise with a fixed matching component partition.

The canonical move maps are the standard local filling identifications, identity outside their specified local neighborhoods. Under exactly this hypothesis, every marked decorated bordism admits an exterior decorated presentation, and two presentations of the same marked decoration are connected by the corresponding undecorated moves, exterior colored graph isotopies, and the open-colored-strand slides in (2).

The hypothesis in (3) concerns the **specified** output identification, not merely existence of some diffeomorphism. No undecorated completeness theorem is proved or assumed silently here. After surgery components are colored by $\Omega$, all the extra graph moves in this conclusion preserve the complete fixed-coupon evaluation by [[lem-kirby-color-full-band-slide-and-coupon-identity]]; the usual local $O1/O2/O3$ normalization identities are separate algebraic suppliers. Connectedness is not required.
For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Then

$$p_+p_-=D^2,\qquad \kappa^{-1}=p_-/D.$$

The formal Kirby color is $\Omega=\sum_i d_i\,i$. A zero-framed $\Omega$ meridian around a simple strand $j$ acts by $D^2\delta_{j,0}$ times the identity, and a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $p_\pm$. Hence the surgery normalization

$$\tau(M_L)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(L_\Omega)$$

is invariant under adding/removing a disjoint $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot; it gives $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$ and $\tau(S^2\times S^1)=1$. The same normalized graph evaluation is invariant under full framed surgery-component handle slides and colored-strand slides over surgery components, with all arbitrary exterior graph coupons retained. A topological theorem asserting completeness of these and relative moves is a separate supplier.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. Write $b_X:\mathbf1\to X\otimes X^*$ and $e_X:X^*\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ for left duality, $r_X=e_{X^*}(j_X\otimes1)$ for right evaluation, and $b_X^R=(1\otimes j_X^{-1})b_{X^*}$ for right coevaluation. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

The zero-framed meridian operator $E_X=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i})$ equals $D^2P_X$, where $P_X$ is the projection onto the full unit-isotypic summand. For $a\in\operatorname{End}(i^*\otimes j)$ define

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]], with finite simple-label set $I$, tensor unit $\mathbf1$, and dual label $i^*$ for each $i$. Define the **handle object**

$$H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*.$$

For an oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$ with ordered marked points labeled by objects $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, fix a parametrization and the standard handle decomposition used to read its labels. The associated algebraic state space is

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}\!\left(\mathbf1,\, W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}\right).$$

The empty tensor product is $\mathbf1$ and $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. Reversing the orientation of a marked boundary circle replaces its label $W$ by the left dual $W^*$. This formula defines a vector space only; mapping-class operators, bordism maps, independence of parametrization, and gluing are not asserted here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. Write $b_X:\mathbf1\to X\otimes X^*$ and $e_X:X^*\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ for left duality, $r_X=e_{X^*}(j_X\otimes1)$ for right evaluation, and $b_X^R=(1\otimes j_X^{-1})b_{X^*}$ for right coevaluation. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by

> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a spherical tensor category over an algebraically closed field $k$, with spherical structure $a$.
For every object $X$ and every endomorphism $x:X\to X$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a_Xx)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(xa_X^{-1}).$$

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

An object is a closed oriented surface $\Sigma$ with a fixed finite collection of marked points carrying simple labels of the complex modular ribbon fusion category, together with a Lagrangian subspace $\lambda\subset H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$ for the signed intersection form. An elementary morphism is an oriented compact smooth 3-bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ with product collars and fixed boundary parametrizations, a properly embedded colored ribbon graph whose ends match the marked labels, and an integer weight $n\in\mathbb Z$. Reversing a boundary orientation dualizes its labels.

For any closed oriented surface $\Sigma$, the intersection convention is $\omega_\Sigma([\alpha],[\beta])=$ the signed intersection number in which the tangent to $\alpha$ followed by the tangent to $\beta$ gives the surface orientation. For a bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$, write $j_r$ for the inclusion maps into $H_1(M;\mathbb R)$ and set

$$\Lambda_M=\{(x_0,x_1)\in H_1(\Sigma_0;\mathbb R)\oplus H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R):j_0x_0=j_1x_1\}.$$

Give the product the form $-\omega_{\Sigma_0}\oplus\omega_{\Sigma_1}$. The boundary-kernel lemma applied to $\partial M$ gives the relation with $j_0x_0=-j_1x_1$; changing the sign of the second coordinate is symplectic and gives exactly $\Lambda_M$. Hence $\Lambda_M$ is Lagrangian ([[lem-3-manifold-boundary-kernel-is-lagrangian]]).

For composable bordisms $M_1:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ and $M_2:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$, put $A=\Lambda_{M_1}$ and $B=\Lambda_{M_2}$. For a relation $R\subseteq\overline V\oplus W$, write $R(L)=\{w:\exists v\in L,(v,w)\in R\}$ and $R^t(Q)=\{v:\exists w\in Q,(v,w)\in R\}$. These use the inclusion maps into each individual bordism. The three Lagrangians for composition lie in the middle surface:

$$K_1=A(\lambda_0),\qquad K_0=\lambda_1,\qquad K_2=B^t(\lambda_2)\quad\subseteq H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R).$$

They are Lagrangian by [[lem-lagrangian-relation-sends-lagrangian-to-lagrangian]], applied also to the transposed relation. With the Wall-form sign fixed in [[lem-maslov-index-four-lagrangian-cocycle]], define

$$n(M_2\circ M_1)=n_2+n_1+\mu(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For mapping cylinders of symplectic maps $f_1,f_2$, the index is $\mu(f_1\lambda_0,\lambda_1,f_2^{-1}\lambda_2)=\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$. This is Walker's prescribed sign and order. For arbitrary bordisms, replacing the individual relations by homology maps into the glued manifold is not part of the definition.

Identity bordisms are cylinders with weight zero. Disjoint union takes the disjoint union of geometric data, the direct sum of the surface Lagrangians, and the sum of weights. The empty surface is the monoidal unit. Bordisms are identified by orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms respecting collars, parametrizations, ribbon data and weights; smoothing glued collars is understood up to these identifications. Associativity and the weight, unit and disjoint-union laws follow from the relation identity in [[lem-maslov-correction-composes-for-lagrangian-relations]] and the proof below. This defines the weighted category before any RT functor is asserted. The equality between its correction and a surgery-signature defect remains a separate obligation of [[thm-weighted-rt-tqft-and-factorization]]; no unweighted TQFT is asserted.

Assume full AC. Let $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ be any compact oriented smooth three-bordism with its fixed product collars, boundary parametrizations and a properly embedded finite colored framed ribbon graph with actual coupon morphisms and the prescribed labeled boundary ribbons. For each connected component of $M$, fix a connected standard base $N$ with exactly that parametrized external boundary: for example the complement in $S^3$ of disjoint standard handlebodies, one of the prescribed genus for each boundary component. Keep these boundary handlebodies, their attaching parametrizations and their marked cap ribbons fixed. A closed component uses $N=S^3$. Take the finite disjoint union with this specified component partition. More generally, any fixed connected compact oriented base with the same marked boundary is allowed on each component.

There is a finite framed link $L\subset\operatorname{int}N$, off the protected boundary collar, an exterior representative of the given colored ribbon graph with all original coupons, and a specified orientation-preserving output identification $N_L\to M$ retaining every boundary parametrization and collar ribbon. Here $N_L$ is the framed Dehn filling of the link exterior. For any two such presentations, the **specified** identification of their outputs is realized up to isotopy fixed on the protected collar by a finite sequence of exterior framed isotopies and the following relative moves:

1. $O1$: insert or delete a split $+1$ or $-1$ framed unknot in an interior ball, with the actual filled-ball identification.
2. $O2$: the specified framed band slide of one surgery component over another, with the full band framing and canonical local filling comparison.
3. $O3$: insert or delete an arbitrary integer-framed knot $K$ and its small meridian $U$ with the disk framing zero; the induced filling identification is the identity outside its solid-torus support.
4. Exterior framed colored graph isotopy and framed slides of open graph strands over the specified surgery-framed longitudes. Every original graph label, coupon morphism, attachment order, boundary ribbon and endpoint remains fixed or is transported by the recorded move map.

Thus the cumulative move map, with its transported graph, realizes the given marked decorated bordism, including its specified output identification. No hypothesis on any fundamental group is imposed. $O3$ is essential in this general fixed-base scope and is not silently replaced by a split Hopf pair or by $O1/O2$ alone. All supports fix the given external collars; no unproved variable-boundary slicing move list is required. Disconnected bordisms, empty input/output surfaces, closed components, empty graphs and the empty bordism are allowed, with the fixed component partition. Any integer weight and object Lagrangians of the weighted ribbon-bordism definition are retained as part of the external data; this is a presentation and move theorem, independently of the later evaluation and anomaly formulas.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]], with finite simple-label set $I$, tensor unit $\mathbf1$, and dual label $i^*$ for each $i$. Define the **handle object**

$$H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*.$$

For an oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$ with ordered marked points labeled by objects $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, fix a parametrization and the standard handle decomposition used to read its labels. The associated algebraic state space is

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}\!\left(\mathbf1,\, W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}\right).$$

The empty tensor product is $\mathbf1$ and $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. Reversing the orientation of a marked boundary circle replaces its label $W$ by the left dual $W^*$. This formula defines a vector space only; mapping-class operators, bordism maps, independence of parametrization, and gluing are not asserted here.

Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. For the state spaces of [[def-rt-state-spaces]], composition is a perfect pairing

$$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X)\times\operatorname{Hom}(X,\mathbf1)\longrightarrow\mathbb C,\qquad(v,w)\longmapsto wv.$$

The categorical trace of $1_{i\otimes i^*}$ is $d_i^2$, and $\operatorname{tr}(1_H)=\sum_i d_i^2=D^2$ for $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$. Distinguish that trace from the actual standard-cap geometric Gram form on a connected genus-$g$ surface:

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i,\qquad N_t|_i=Q_t^{-1}|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1.$$

Here $i$ is the full handle-color tuple, $d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}$, and the inverse is in composition-dual coordinates. For disconnected surfaces take tensor products and empty value $\mathbb C$.

For every compact parametrized colored ribbon bordism, capping against all testing states, taking the surgery-color sum with closed normalization $D^{-m-b_0(M)}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$, and applying $N_{\rm out}$ defines a unique linear map $Z_\alpha(M)$. It is independent of the marked surgery presentation, all auxiliary coupon bases and their complete identity resolutions. It retains the prescribed boundary caps, parametrizations, colors and actual coupon morphisms. These maps satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws, and the actual stacked-presentation law of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]]. The identification of its signature defect with the Maslov correction is a separate supplier.

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

Assume AC, carried through Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. Use outward-normal-first boundary orientations and the Walker Maslov form: on triples $a_1+a_2+a_3=0$, $a_i\in L_i$, it is $\psi(a,a')=\omega(a_1,a_2')$, with signature $\mu_W(L_1,L_2,L_3)$ after removing the radical.

If an oriented four-manifold is decomposed as $W=W_1\cup_{M_0}W_2$, with

$$\partial W_1=M_0\cup(-M_1),\qquad\partial W_2=(-M_0)\cup M_2,\qquad\Sigma=\partial M_0=\partial M_1=\partial M_2,$$

put $K_i=\ker[H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)\to H_1(M_i;\mathbb R)]$. Then

$$\sigma(W)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)-\mu_W(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For the actual standard-cap special-graph stacking presentations of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], let $\alpha_q$ be the meridian Lagrangians of the chosen reference caps and $R_q$ the individual bordism homology relations. With the canonical middle-object orientation, the actual surgery signatures satisfy

$$\Delta\sigma:=\sigma(B_{\rm comp})-\sigma(B_1)-\sigma(B_2)=\mu_W(R_1\alpha_0,\alpha_1,R_2^t\alpha_2)=:\mu_\alpha.$$

For arbitrary real object Lagrangians $\lambda_q$, define the actual cap-reference integer

$$a(R;\lambda,\alpha)=-\mu_W(\lambda_0,\alpha_0,R^t\alpha_1)-\mu_W(R\lambda_0,\alpha_1,\lambda_1).$$

It satisfies $a(BA)-a(B)-a(A)=\mu_\alpha-\mu_\lambda$, where $\mu_\lambda=\mu_W(A\lambda_0,\lambda_1,B^t\lambda_2)$. Consequently the correctly weighted operators are

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)}Z_\alpha(M),\qquad n_{\rm comp}=n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda.$$

They compose strictly, preserve the identity and tensor laws, and a unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. In particular the action $\kappa^{-n}$ is incompatible with this prescribed $+\mu_W$ composition and the fixed surgery normalization $\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$. These are normalization/signature claims for the indicated presentations; the full relative surgery/Cerf completeness theorem remains separate.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category and its state-space convention in [[def-rt-state-spaces]], with $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$ and $S=s/D$. On a disconnected surface take the tensor product of the connected Hom state spaces, with empty value $\mathbb C$. Write $r_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $b_i^R:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$ for the corresponding right evaluation and coevaluation. With fixed tensor order and parametrizations, separating sewing is the isomorphism

$$G:\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes i)\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes Y),\qquad G_i(f\otimes k)=(1_X\otimes r_i\otimes1_Y)(f\otimes k).$$

For any simple-summand inclusions $g_{i\alpha}:i^*\to X$ and composition-dual projections $p_{i\alpha}:X\to i^*$, its inverse is

$$F(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}((g_{i\alpha}\otimes1_i)b_i^R)\otimes((p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z).$$

For nonseparating sewing the direct-sum inclusions/projections $u_i:i\otimes i^*\to H$, $v_i:H\to i\otimes i^*$ give mutually inverse maps

$$G((z_i)_i)=\sum_i(1_X\otimes u_i)z_i,\qquad F(z)=((1_X\otimes v_i)z)_i.$$

These maps retain every multiplicity coordinate, are independent of auxiliary bases, are natural on uncut factors, and commute for disjoint cut pairs with fixed compatible tensor order. Thus iterated algebraic sewing has the explicit reverse cutting inverse. For simple marked labels,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i_1\otimes\cdots\otimes i_n\otimes H^{\otimes g})=\sum_x S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^n S_{i_rx}.$$

These are algebraic state-space identities. Identification with presentation-independent bordism sewing requires the separately constructed RT functor; no surgery move theorem is a hypothesis or conclusion here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular spherical ribbon fusion category. Put $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, choose $D\ne0$, let $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, and $\Omega=\sum_i d_i i$. Write $b_X:\mathbf1\to X\otimes X^*$ and $e_X:X^*\otimes X\to\mathbf1$ for left duality, $r_X=e_{X^*}(j_X\otimes1)$ for right evaluation, and $b_X^R=(1\otimes j_X^{-1})b_{X^*}$ for right coevaluation. For $a:X\otimes Z\to Y\otimes Z$ define

$$\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)=(1_Y\otimes r_Z)(a\otimes1_{Z^*})(1_X\otimes b_Z),\qquad M_{X,Z}=c_{Z,X}c_{X,Z}.$$

Then $p_+p_-=D^2$, and the following are identities of complete morphisms, valid with arbitrary exterior tensor factors and coupons:

$$K_\pm(X):=\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i}^{\pm1})=p_\pm\theta_X^{\mp1}.$$

The zero-framed meridian operator $E_X=\sum_i d_i\operatorname{ptr}_i(M_{X,i})$ equals $D^2P_X$, where $P_X$ is the projection onto the full unit-isotypic summand. For $a\in\operatorname{End}(i^*\otimes j)$ define

$$R_{ij}(a)=(r_i\otimes1_j\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes1_{i^*}\otimes b_j).$$

The paired-handle/coupon contraction is

$$R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})=\delta_{ij}\frac{D^2}{d_i}1_{i\otimes i^*}.$$

Thus the normalized graph evaluation $D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F$ is unchanged under a signed generalized Fenn–Rourke twist-surgery move or circumcision adding a framed knot and its small zero-framed meridian. These are local algebraic identities; a complete presentation/move theorem is a separate topological assertion. No positivity, unitary conjugation, or anomaly cancellation is assumed.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Let $(-)^{\vee\vee}$ be the monoidal endofunctor of
[[thm-the-double-dual-is-a-monoidal-functor]].

A **pivotal structure** on a rigid monoidal category is an isomorphism of
monoidal functors

$$a:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^{\vee\vee}.$$

Equivalently, it is a natural family of isomorphisms
$a_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^{\vee\vee}$ such that

$$a_{X\otimes Y}=a_X\otimes a_Y,\qquad a_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$$

after transporting along the monoidal structure of the double-dual functor.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

Let $u$ and $v$ be parenthesised tensor words on the same ordered letters
$x_1,\dots,x_n$. Then there exists a unique canonical natural isomorphism
$E_u\Rightarrow E_v$. Equivalently, any two canonical morphisms from $u$ to $v$
are equal.

$$N_iS=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{S_{ix}}{S_{0x}}\right)_{x\in I}.$$

This is the algebraic formula; no complex conjugation is used.

$$s^2=D^2C.$$
