No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively. A normalized **abelian 3-cocycle** is a pair of functions $\omega:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ and $r:G^2\to\mathbb C^\times$, equal to $1$ whenever one of their arguments is $0$, satisfying the pentagon equation

$$\omega(a,b,c)\omega(a,b+c,d)\omega(b,c,d)=\omega(a+b,c,d)\omega(a,b,c+d)$$

and the two braided hexagon equations

$$\omega(b,c,a)\omega(a,b,c)r(a,b+c)=r(a,b)r(a,c)\omega(b,a,c),$$

$$r(a+b,c)=\omega(a,b,c)\omega(c,a,b)\omega(a,c,b)^{-1}r(a,c)r(b,c).$$

The associated pointed category has one simple object $g$ in each grade $g\in G$, tensor product $g\otimes h=g+h$, associator $\alpha_{g,h,k}:(g\otimes h)\otimes k\to g\otimes(h\otimes k)$ given by scalar $\omega(g,h,k)$, and braiding $c_{g,h}:g\otimes h\to h\otimes g$ given by scalar $r(g,h)$. For the left dual $g^\vee=-g$, take evaluation $g^\vee\otimes g\to0$ to have scalar $1$ and coevaluation $0\to g\otimes g^\vee$ to have scalar $\omega(g,-g,g)^{-1}$. The first snake is the identity by this choice; the second is the identity because the normalized pentagon at $(g,-g,g,-g)$ gives $\omega(g,-g,g)\omega(-g,g,-g)=1$. A ribbon twist is a function $q:G\to\mathbb C^\times$ with $q(0)=1$, $q(-g)=q(g)$, and

$$q(g+h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)q(g)q(h).$$

Write $b(g,h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)$ for the double-braiding scalar. The pointed ribbon category data include a compatible pivotal structure whose twist is $q$ and whose simple dimensions are $1$; this convention is an explicit input, not a consequence of the quadratic function alone. [[thm-pointed-metric-group-is-modular-iff-radical-trivial]] proves from the two hexagons that $b$ is a symmetric bicharacter and that the Hopf-link matrix has entries $s_{gh}=b(g,h)$. A quadratic function alone is not the category data: the associator, both hexagons, duality maps, and the stated pivotal convention are part of the definition.

Let $(G,\omega,r,q)$ be pointed ribbon data as in [[def-pointed-metric-group-ribbon-category]], and let $b(g,h)=r(g,h)r(h,g)$. The associated pointed ribbon fusion category is modular if and only if

$$\operatorname{rad}(b)=\{g\in G:b(g,h)=1\text{ for every }h\in G\}=\{0\}.$$

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category and its state-space convention in [[def-rt-state-spaces]], with $H=\bigoplus_i i\otimes i^*$ and $S=s/D$. On a disconnected surface take the tensor product of the connected Hom state spaces, with empty value $\mathbb C$. Write $r_i:i\otimes i^*\to\mathbf1$ and $b_i^R:\mathbf1\to i^*\otimes i$ for the corresponding right evaluation and coevaluation. With fixed tensor order and parametrizations, separating sewing is the isomorphism

$$G:\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes i)\otimes\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X\otimes Y),\qquad G_i(f\otimes k)=(1_X\otimes r_i\otimes1_Y)(f\otimes k).$$

For any simple-summand inclusions $g_{i\alpha}:i^*\to X$ and composition-dual projections $p_{i\alpha}:X\to i^*$, its inverse is

$$F(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}((g_{i\alpha}\otimes1_i)b_i^R)\otimes((p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z).$$

For nonseparating sewing the direct-sum inclusions/projections $u_i:i\otimes i^*\to H$, $v_i:H\to i\otimes i^*$ give mutually inverse maps

$$G((z_i)_i)=\sum_i(1_X\otimes u_i)z_i,\qquad F(z)=((1_X\otimes v_i)z)_i.$$

These maps retain every multiplicity coordinate, are independent of auxiliary bases, are natural on uncut factors, and commute for disjoint cut pairs with fixed compatible tensor order. Thus iterated algebraic sewing has the explicit reverse cutting inverse. For simple marked labels,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i_1\otimes\cdots\otimes i_n\otimes H^{\otimes g})=\sum_x S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^n S_{i_rx}.$$

These are algebraic state-space identities. Identification with presentation-independent bordism sewing requires the separately constructed RT functor; no surgery move theorem is a hypothesis or conclusion here.

Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. Let $\mathcal C$ be any complex modular ribbon fusion category, with fixed $D\ne0$, $\kappa=p_+/D$, the state spaces of [[def-rt-state-spaces]] and the weighted collared ribbon-bordism category of [[def-weighted-lagrangian-ribbon-bordism]]. No unitarity, positivity or anomaly-cancellation hypothesis is imposed. For each parametrized connected boundary surface choose its standard spine caps, with meridian Lagrangian $\alpha$; the object may carry any real Lagrangian $\lambda$. Use the Walker Maslov convention and actual cap-reference correction $a(R;\lambda,\alpha)$ of [[lem-wall-signature-and-rt-cap-reference-correction]].

A connected surgery presentation with $m$ surgery components, linking matrix $B$ and integer bordism weight $n$ has the exact outgoing color-block operator

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)^j_i=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $F_0$ is the finite colored graph operator with the disconnected-boundary unit-channel projections of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], and $d(j)$ is the product of outgoing handle-color dimensions. For disconnected $M$ use the product over its connected components, equivalently replace $-m-1$ by $-m-b_0(M)$; the external weight contributes the single factor $\kappa^n$. The empty value is $\mathbb C$.

These maps are independent of all marked surgery presentations and auxiliary coupon bases and define a symmetric monoidal functor on the full specified weighted category, including actual colored coupons, disconnected bordisms and empty ends. The functor preserves duality. A unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. No ordinary anomaly-free functor is asserted without cancellation of this anomaly.

For every compatible circle cut there is a natural factorization isomorphism

$$V(\Sigma_{\rm glued};\vec W)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}V(\Sigma_{\rm cut};\vec W,i,i^*).$$

The sewing map from right to left is the actual normalized tube map; its inverse is the complete composition-dual cutting resolution. Both separating and nonseparating cuts, all multiplicities, commuting disjoint cuts and iterated gluing are included. Markings, tensor order and the Lagrangian identifications of the cut are retained; a change of parametrization is represented by its weighted mapping cylinder.

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

Assume AC, carried through Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. Use outward-normal-first boundary orientations and the Walker Maslov form: on triples $a_1+a_2+a_3=0$, $a_i\in L_i$, it is $\psi(a,a')=\omega(a_1,a_2')$, with signature $\mu_W(L_1,L_2,L_3)$ after removing the radical.

If an oriented four-manifold is decomposed as $W=W_1\cup_{M_0}W_2$, with

$$\partial W_1=M_0\cup(-M_1),\qquad\partial W_2=(-M_0)\cup M_2,\qquad\Sigma=\partial M_0=\partial M_1=\partial M_2,$$

put $K_i=\ker[H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)\to H_1(M_i;\mathbb R)]$. Then

$$\sigma(W)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)-\mu_W(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For the actual standard-cap special-graph stacking presentations of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], let $\alpha_q$ be the meridian Lagrangians of the chosen reference caps and $R_q$ the individual bordism homology relations. With the canonical middle-object orientation, the actual surgery signatures satisfy

$$\Delta\sigma:=\sigma(B_{\rm comp})-\sigma(B_1)-\sigma(B_2)=\mu_W(R_1\alpha_0,\alpha_1,R_2^t\alpha_2)=:\mu_\alpha.$$

For arbitrary real object Lagrangians $\lambda_q$, define the actual cap-reference integer

$$a(R;\lambda,\alpha)=-\mu_W(\lambda_0,\alpha_0,R^t\alpha_1)-\mu_W(R\lambda_0,\alpha_1,\lambda_1).$$

It satisfies $a(BA)-a(B)-a(A)=\mu_\alpha-\mu_\lambda$, where $\mu_\lambda=\mu_W(A\lambda_0,\lambda_1,B^t\lambda_2)$. Consequently the correctly weighted operators are

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)}Z_\alpha(M),\qquad n_{\rm comp}=n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda.$$

They compose strictly, preserve the identity and tensor laws, and a unit increase of weight acts by $\kappa$. In particular the action $\kappa^{-n}$ is incompatible with this prescribed $+\mu_W$ composition and the fixed surgery normalization $\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}$. These are normalization/signature claims for the indicated presentations; the full relative surgery/Cerf completeness theorem remains separate.

Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space and let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be Lagrangian subspaces. Put

$$U_{123}=\frac{L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)}{(L_1\cap L_2)+(L_1\cap L_3)}.$$

For $a\in L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)$ write $a+b+c=0$ with $b\in L_2,c\in L_3$. The form

$$\psi_{123}([a],[a'])=\omega(a,b')$$

is well-defined, symmetric, and nondegenerate. Define $\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)=\operatorname{sign}(\psi_{123})$. For any four Lagrangians,

$$\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)+\mu(L_1,L_3,L_4)=\mu(L_1,L_2,L_4)+\mu(L_2,L_3,L_4).$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $\ell\ge3$, $t=\pi/\ell$, and suppose a spherical ribbon fusion category has simple labels $a=0,\ldots,\ell-2$ with

$$N_{ab}^c=1\quad\text{for }c=|a-b|,|a-b|+2,\ldots,\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b),$$

and all other $N_{ab}^c=0$, with $d_a=\sin((a+1)t)/\sin t$ and $\theta_a=e^{it\,a(a+2)/2}$. Then

$$s_{ab}=\frac{\sin((a+1)(b+1)t)}{\sin t},\qquad D^2=\frac{\ell}{2\sin^2t},\qquad S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac2\ell}\sin((a+1)(b+1)t).$$

The sine matrix is invertible and $S^2=I$. This is a conditional calculation from the displayed category data; it does not assert that a particular tilting quotient has those data.

Fix an integer $\ell\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\ell$. Use the divided-power integral form of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], specialized by $v\mapsto q$ to $\mathbb C$. In type $A_1$, write $K=K_h$ and $E,F$ for the rank-one generators. The convention is

$$KEK^{-1}=q^2E,\qquad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F,\qquad [E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}},$$

$$\Delta(K)=K\otimes K,\qquad \Delta(E)=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,\qquad \Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F.$$

This is the Sawin coproduct, rather than the inverse-$K$ coproduct in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Its counit is $\varepsilon(K)=1$, $\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon(F)=0$ and its antipode is $S(E)=-EK^{-1}$, $S(F)=-KF$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\rm target}=KE_{\rm lib}$, $F_{\rm target}=F_{\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\rm target}=K_{\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.

The Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. A finite-dimensional module is **type 1** when it carries its integral-weight grading $M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}M_m$ with $K|_{M_m}=q^m$, the full toral character $T_{c,t}|_{M_m}=\begin{bmatrix}m+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q I$ for every $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$, and $E^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m+2r}$, $F^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m-2r}$. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue. Every module intertwiner preserves it: for $m<n$, $T_{-m,n-m}$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $1$ on weights $m$ and $n$.

For $a\ge0$, the Weyl module $\Delta(a)$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ and actions

$$Kv_j=q^{a-2j}v_j,\qquad E^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}a-j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j-r},\qquad F^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j+r},$$

where the Gaussian binomials are the Laurent-polynomial specializations of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and $v_j=0$ outside $0\le j\le a$. Its dual is the dual Weyl module $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. A **Weyl filtration** (respectively dual-Weyl filtration) is a finite submodule filtration whose successive quotients are modules $\Delta(a)$ (respectively $\nabla(a)$). A **tilting module** is a module with both filtrations.

Take $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, so $s^2=q$. The ribbon category is the full weight-lattice extension $\mathcal U_s^\dagger(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of this Lusztig form, not its root-lattice restriction. Its toral factor is the completed function algebra on the weight lattice $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, acting on each weight space by its weight character. Before specialization, the rank-one universal $R$-matrix is the Sawin weight-lattice expression

$R=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E^{(r)}\otimes F^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$

interpreted in the completed tensor product; at the root it means the image of the integral completed form, not termwise division by a vanishing $[r]_q!$. In ordinary powers the coefficient is $q^{r(r-1)/2}(q-q^{-1})^r/[r]_q!$; changing to two divided powers multiplies that coefficient by $([r]_q!)^2$. Thus the displayed divided-power coefficient is Laurent integral and vanishes for $r\ge\ell$ after specialization. The toral factor is the weight pairing, fixed explicitly by $D$ above. The pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and the twist is $\theta=u^{-1}j$ for the Drinfeld map $u$. The object class of this page is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for this weight-lattice ribbon extension. No assertion about semisimplicity or the trace radical is part of this definition.

Use the full integral-weight divided-power category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], with $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$ and every $\ell\ge3$. The displayed strings define $\Delta(a)$, and $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. For all $a,b\ge0$,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=\delta_{ab},\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=0.$$

Here Ext vanishing means that every short exact sequence in the finite-dimensional full-weight category with those end terms splits. The tensor product $\Delta(a)\otimes\Delta(b)$ has one Weyl factor of each label $a+b,a+b-2,\ldots,|a-b|$, and the analogous dual-Weyl assertion holds. Both filtration classes are closed under direct summands. Thus tiltings are closed under tensor products, duals and direct summands. For every $a\ge0$ there is exactly one indecomposable tilting $T(a)$ of highest weight $a$; its weight-$a$ space is one-dimensional, and it occurs as a summand of $V^{\otimes a}$, where $V=\Delta(1)$. Every finite tilting is a finite direct sum of these $T(a)$, so the additive idempotent-complete tensor category generated by $V$ is the entire tilting category.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and use the full-weight category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Write $T(m)$ for the indecomposable tilting of highest weight $m$ and $\chi(m)=\sum_{j=0}^m e^{m-2j}$. For $a\ge1$ and $0\le b\le\ell-2$,

$$\operatorname{ch}T(a\ell+b)=\chi(a\ell+b)+\chi(a\ell-b-2),\qquad \operatorname{ch}T(a\ell-1)=\chi(a\ell-1).$$

Also $T(m)=\Delta(m)=\nabla(m)$ for $0\le m<\ell$. With the positive $K$ pivotal map, the dimension on a Weyl character is $[m+1]_q$. Consequently every $T(m)$ with $m\ge\ell-1$ has zero pivotal trace on **every** endomorphism, so its identity is negligible. In the retained range $0\le m\le\ell-2$, $T(m)$ is simple of nonzero pivotal dimension $[m+1]_q$.

For every $\ell\ge3$, let $\mathcal T_\ell$ be the full finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], and $\mathcal N_\ell$ its negligible ideal. The quotient with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(X,Y)/\mathcal N_\ell(X,Y)$ is a finite semisimple ribbon category. Its simple objects are exactly $T(0),\ldots,T(\ell-2)$, of pivotal dimensions $[a+1]_q$, and

$$[T(a)][T(b)]=\sum_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}[T(c)]\qquad(0\le a,b\le\ell-2).$$

Here a fusion category means a $\mathbb C$-linear rigid semisimple monoidal category with simple unit and finitely many simple isomorphism classes. The quotient is spherical with the specified positive pivotal dimensions and inherits the full ribbon structure, including even $\ell$.

For every $\ell\ge3$, the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] is rigid and braided by $c_{M,N}=\operatorname{flip}\circ R_{M,N}$, where

$$R_{M,N}=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E_M^{(r)}\otimes F_N^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$$

The sum is finite on every pair of objects. Its pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and its ribbon twist is $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}j_M$, with $u$ the Drinfeld map. For $V=\Delta(1)$, the self-dual cup and cap are

$$w=v_+\otimes v_- -q^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+,\qquad b(v_+\otimes v_-)=-q,\quad b(v_-\otimes v_+)=1,$$

with $b(v_\pm\otimes v_\pm)=0$. They obey both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$ for $j$. Nevertheless $\dim_j V=\delta$. If $U=-wb$, then $U^2=\delta U$, the adjacent TL relations hold, and

$$c_{V,V}=sI-s^{-1}U,\qquad T=qU-I=-s\,c_{V,V}^{-1}.$$

The $\Delta(2)$ and trivial channels have crossing eigenvalues $s,-s^{-3}$ and Hecke eigenvalues $-1,q^2$, respectively. Their twists are $s^8,1$; $\theta_V=s^3I$. The $\Delta(2)$ channel is removed in the negligible quotient when $\ell=3$. More generally $\theta_{\Delta(a)}=s^{a(a+2)}I$ for $0\le a\le\ell-1$. These assertions include even $\ell$ and use no small-quantum-group substitution.

Use all $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Put $V=\Delta(1)$ and let $P_0$ be its trivial-channel projector in $V\otimes V=\Delta(2)\oplus\Delta(0)$. The maps

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. The highest-weight-$2$ channel is retained only when $\ell\ge4$. Pivotal traces, twists and all framed ribbon closures agree under the stated corrected comparison. Assume countable choice only when invoking the cited free framed-tangle evaluation theorem; the local matrix and path arguments use no choice axiom.

For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$.
